thread:
Sam: quick check — we have a planned release cutover at 2200 UTC tonight that touches tf modules: network/vpc, iam/roles, and infra/edge-gw. need a short canary plan + explicit rollback steps. who owns the rollback lifeboat?
Maya: I can own the canary for vpc changes. proposing a single-AZ canary (staging-a) first, then burst to prod if green.
Liam: tagging in deploy bot to run a dry-run plan now and confirm provider versions are pinned. @DeployBot run preflight for branch release/forge-2026
DeployBot: preflight started for commit sha: b3f7a9c. Running `terraform init -upgrade=false` then `terraform plan -var-file=release/forge.tfvars`. Lockfile present: provider v4.2.1, module network v1.3.0 (pinned).
DeployBot: plan summary: 7 to add, 2 to change, 1 to destroy. Risk flags: IAM role attach changes detected — manual review required.
Nisha: thanks — that's the important bit. we should avoid simultaneous role changes + route table rewrites. plan to sequence: 1) VPC canary, 2) route tables, 3) IAM attach.
Sam: agreed. also add an explicit module pin in root module before apply: `module "network" { source = "./modules/network" version = "1.3.0" }` and put rollback mutex note in release notes.
Maya: for rollback lifeboat — my play: if canary fails, revert by `git revert b3f7a9c` + `terraform apply -target=module.network -var-file=release/forge.tfvars` in staging to reinstantiate previous network state, then gate prod.
Liam: small nit — don't `-target` destroy; better to reapply previous state from the revert commit. we keep a pre-apply snapshot (state export) for staging. I can run the snapshot and store it in S3: `aws s3 cp state-staging.json s3://redwood-ops/state-backups/forge-2026-staging.json`.
Sam: perfect. add the rollback checklist to the runbook: 1) stop traffic to canary AZ (k8s node drain + LB weight 0), 2) revert commit, 3) run `terraform apply` against staging, 4) verify connectivity & IAM-binding counts, 5) only then proceed to prod.
DeployBot: preflight success — no drift detected. Plan file: /tmp/plan-b3f7a9c.out. ETA for scheduled window: 2200-2230 UTC.
Maya: I'll start the canary at 2200. tagging oncall: @oncall-bot please hold pager for 2200-2230 and escalate to infra-sre if rollback invoked.
oncall-bot: acknowledged — oncall temporarily muted for that window. reminder set.
Liam: will run a `terraform apply -auto-approve -parallelism=10 -lock=true` for the canary AZ only. paste snippet for the run:
```
export TF_VAR_region=us-west-2
git checkout b3f7a9c
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tfstate" -upgrade=false
terraform plan -out=plan-canary.out -var-file=release/forge.tfvars -target=module.network["staging-a"]
terraform apply plan-canary.out
```
Maya: +1. after apply I'll run smoke checks: ping gateway, curl metadata endpoint, and run `aws iam get-role` to check bindings.
Nisha: I'll watch metrics: route53 latency, LB error rates, and IAM attach logs. will post a green/red within 5m.
Sam: if green, we proceed with a controlled prod apply (stagger AZs, 5m between each). if red, follow rollback lifeboat and abort cutover. add note in release notes: "network/iam changes pinned to module v1.3.0; rollback procedure requires revert and reapply from commit b3f7a9c"
DeployBot: scheduled apply queued at 2200 UTC. webhook: https://deploybot.internal/redwood/ops/queues/1722233344
Liam: I also added a short terraform plan check in CI: ensure `provider` block matches lockfile, fail if drift.
Maya: thanks — we'll keep chan updates brief. I'll post statuses: `CANARY START`, `CANARY OK` or `CANARY FAIL` and actions we took.
Sam: perfect. final reminder: no IAM role detach in the same wave as route table rewrites. escalate immediately if unexpected detaches appear. :rotating_light:
Nisha: noted. making the postmortem stub in advance in release notes doc.
Sam: thanks everyone. ping me if you need to abort — I'll coordinate customer comms. :thumbsup:
